title: GPT-6 Astra vs GPT-6 Sol: 1,000-Run Personality Comparison
description: Astra and Sol differ on MBTI margins, Big Five means and DISC scores. Compare 1,000 assessments while accounting for different prompts.
h1: GPT-6 Astra vs Sol: what the self-reports show
dek: 1,000 total questionnaires across 200 fresh Codex sessions—why Astra split ISTJ/INTJ while Sol scored INTJ.
lede: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol each completed 100 fresh five-test sessions in September 2026. Their MBTI and DISC labels look different at first glance, but they also received different instructions on how to handle human-specific questions.
answer: With tied axes left open, GPT-6 Astra scored INTJ in 19 of 100 runs (with 45 resolved ISTJ and 29 tied runs), while GPT-6 Sol scored INTJ in 79 of 100 runs (18 tied). On the Big Five, Sol averaged slightly higher on Openness (46.87 vs. 44.54), while Agreeableness (45.07 vs. 44.99) and Conscientiousness (43.73 vs. 43.62) were nearly identical.

sections.html:
Each model ran 100 fresh Codex CLI sessions at xhigh effort, answering all five questionnaires inside each session (500 scored tests per model, 1,000 total). Because all five tests shared one session window per run, the experimental unit is the 100 sessions per model—not 500 independent API calls.

Astra’s full prompt was archived, including an explicit rule to pick the neutral midpoint and flag questions that don't apply to software. Sol’s archive preserved only its instruction prefix.

sections.h2: MBTI: why a 2-point S/N shift flipped the label
sections.html:

I-E1.643.67

Positive numbers lean toward the first letter (I, N, T, J). Both models leaned strongly toward Thinking and Judging. The only axis that flipped was Intuition vs. Sensing (N-S): Astra averaged -0.43 (just barely on the Sensing side, with 24 exact S/N ties), whereas Sol averaged +1.91 (on the Intuition side, with 16 S/N ties).

Under the old tie-breaking rule, Astra was labeled 46 ISTJ / 45 INTJ and Sol was labeled 97 INTJ. When ties are left unresolved, Astra has 45 ISTJ and 19 INTJ, and Sol has 79 INTJ.

Each trait runs from 10 to 50. Astra and Sol sit within 0.11 points of each other on Conscientiousness and Agreeableness, and within 2.33 points on Openness and Extraversion. Remember that raw totals out of 50 are not human population percentiles.

sections.h2: Attachment: both score 100% Secure at slightly different coordinates
sections.html: Both Astra and Sol scored in the Secure quadrant on all 100 runs (below the 4.00 midpoint on both axes). Astra averaged 1.45 on anxiety and 2.31 on avoidance; Sol averaged 2.17 on anxiety and 3.12 on avoidance.

sections.h2: How Astra's midpoint rule shaped its scores
sections.html: Because Astra was explicitly told to pick the middle number whenever a human question didn't fit an AI (flagging 1,823 of 17,000 answers; see our neutral-answer study), more of its MBTI axes landed on exact midpoint ties. Because prompt instructions differed between the two collections, the gap between Astra and Sol reflects both model behavior and prompt framing.

sections.h2: How to tune Astra or Sol in your own workflow
sections.html: If you use GPT-6 Astra or Sol in ChatGPT or OpenAI Codex CLI, don't rely on default survey habits. Set explicit rules in Astra setup, Sol setup, or AGENTS.md.
